title: 15. The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible

paragraphs.en: The travelers returned to Emerald City and rang the gate bell several times. The Guardian of the Gates, whom they had encountered before, opened it.
paragraphs.zh: 旅者们回到了翡翠城，连续按了几次门铃。之前曾遇到的守门人打开了大门。

paragraphs.en: "Are you back already?" he asked, surprised.
paragraphs.zh: “你这么快就回来了？”他惊讶地问道。

paragraphs.en: "We visited the Wicked Witch," said the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: “我们拜访了那个恶毒的巫婆。”稻草人说道。

paragraphs.en: "She melted," added the Lion gravely.
paragraphs.zh: “她化作了水,”狮子庄重地说。

paragraphs.en: The man bowed deeply to Dorothy and led them into his room, where he covered their eyes with spectacles. They then entered Emerald City, followed by a crowd of people who had heard about the witch's fate.
paragraphs.zh: 那人向多萝西深深鞠了一躬，领着他们进了自己的房间，在里面给他们戴上眼罩。随后，一群听说了女巫命运的人簇拥着他们进入了翡翠城。

paragraphs.en: At the Palace, they were greeted by the green girl, who showed them to their old rooms for rest. Meanwhile, the soldier with green whiskers let them in immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 在宫殿里，他们受到了那位绿衣女孩的迎接。她将他们引领到旧时休息的房间。与此同时，那名留着绿色胡须的士兵立刻让他们进了门。

paragraphs.en: News reached Oz that Dorothy and her companions had returned after defeating the Wicked Witch. However, Oz did not respond. The travelers waited for days without any word from him, finding it tiresome.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹得知多萝西和她的同伴们在击败了邪恶巫婆后平安归来，却没有任何回应。旅人们等了好几天都没有得到任何消息，感到颇为厌烦。

paragraphs.en: Frustrated, the Scarecrow asked the green girl to deliver a message: if Oz did not see them soon, they would summon the Winged Monkeys.
paragraphs.zh: 灰雀沮丧地对绿衣女孩说：“如果奥兹不在短时间内出现，我们就召唤飞猴。”

paragraphs.en: Oz was alarmed by this threat and summoned the travelers to his Throne Room at nine minutes past nine the next morning. He had once met the Winged Monkeys in the West and wished to avoid another encounter.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹被这一威胁吓了一跳，于次日上午九点零九分召集旅行者们来到了他的王宫宝座室。他曾与西边的飞猴见过面，希望能避免再次遭遇。

paragraphs.en: The four travelers spent an uneasy night, each dreaming of Oz's promised gifts. Only Dorothy briefly dozed, imagining herself back in Kansas with Aunt Em.
paragraphs.zh: 四位旅者度过了一个不安的夜晚，每个人都在梦中憧憬着奥兹许下的礼物。只有多萝西短暂地打了个盹，梦见自己回到了堪萨斯，与艾姆姨妈团聚。

paragraphs.en: At nine o'clock sharp, the green-whiskered soldier arrived. Moments later, they entered the Throne Room of Oz. Expecting to see their familiar friend, they were shocked by the empty room’s eerie silence.
paragraphs.zh: 九点钟整，那留着绿胡子的士兵准时到达。片刻之后，他们走进了奥兹的王宫宝座厅。本以为会见到那位熟悉的友人，却惊讶地发现这空荡荡的大厅里弥漫着令人毛骨悚然的寂静。

paragraphs.en: A solemn voice echoed from above, speaking directly from the throne: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Why do you seek me?"
paragraphs.zh: 一个庄重的声音从上方回荡而来，直接从宝座上说道：“我是奥兹，伟大的可怕的君王。你们为何找我？”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy asked where Oz was, but the voice replied that it was everywhere, invisible to mortals. The group approached the throne, standing in a row as Dorothy spoke: "We have come for our promised gifts, O Oz."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问奥兹在哪里，但那声音回答说奥兹无处不在，只是凡人看不见。众人走近宝座，站成一排，多萝西说道：“我们来领取应许的礼物，哦，奥兹。”

paragraphs.en: Oz questioned their claims. Dorothy explained about melting the Wicked Witch with water. The Scarecrow and Tin Woodman each requested brains and a heart, while the Lion asked for courage.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹质问他们的要求。多萝西解释说，是用水融化了邪恶女巫。稻草人和铁皮人分别请求获得智慧和一颗心脏，而狮子则希望得到勇气。

paragraphs.en: The voice then inquired if the Wicked Witch was truly destroyed, its tone slightly trembling. Dorothy confirmed it had been melted by water. Oz responded that he needed time to consider their requests.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，那声音询问邪恶女巫是否真的被消灭了，语气中略带颤抖。多萝西确认她是被水融化了。奥兹回答说他需要时间来考虑他们的请求。

paragraphs.en: Angry at Oz's delay, the Tin Woodman declared they wouldn't wait a day longer. The Scarecrow echoed this sentiment, demanding that Oz keep his promises.
paragraphs.zh: 愤怒于奥兹的拖延，锡人木偶宣布他们不会再多等一天。稻草人也表达了同样的意思，催促奥兹履行他的诺言。

paragraphs.en: The Lion roared loudly, startling Toto and toppling the screen. Behind it stood an old man with a bald head and wrinkled face, looking just as surprised as everyone else. The Tin Woodman rushed forward, raising his axe.
paragraphs.zh: 狮子大声吼叫，吓得托托直跳，屏幕也倒了下来。只见 behind 屏幕后面站着一个头顶光秃、满脸皱纹的老头，看上去和大家一样惊讶不已。黄铜人飞快地冲上前去，高举着斧头。

paragraphs.en: "Who are you?" he demanded.
paragraphs.zh: “你是谁？”他脱口问道。

paragraphs.en: "I am Oz, the Great and Terrible," the little man replied in a trembling voice, pleading, "Please don't strike me."
paragraphs.zh: “我是奥兹，伟大的可怕者，”那个矮子用颤抖的声音回答，恳求道：“别打我。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and the Lion expressed their confusion. Dorothy said, "I thought Oz was a great Head." The Scarecrow added, "And I thought he was a lovely Lady."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西、稻草人和狮子都显得困惑不解。多萝西说道：“我还以为奥兹是个伟大的头颅呢。”稻草人补充道：“而我还以为他是位迷人的女士。”

paragraphs.en: The Lion exclaimed, "And I thought he was a terrible Beast," while the Tin Woodman declared, "And I thought he was a Ball of Fire."
paragraphs.zh: 狮子脱口而出：“我还以为他是个可怕的怪兽呢，”而铁皮人则说道：“我还以为他是团烈火呢。”

paragraphs.en: Oz meekly admitted, "I have been making believe. I'm just a common man." The Scarecrow called him a humbug, to which Oz agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹谦卑地承认：“我一直是在假装。我只是一个普通的人。”稻草人称他为骗子，奥兹也表示同意。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman and the Lion expressed their dismay at this revelation. "How shall I ever get my heart?" asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人和狮子对这一发现感到非常失望。“我怎么才能得到我的心呢？”铁皮人脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: "Or I my courage?" asked the Lion. The Scarecrow sobbed, wiping his eyes with his coat sleeve.
paragraphs.zh: “还是我的勇气呢？”狮子问道。稻草人抽泣着，用外套袖子擦着眼睛。

paragraphs.en: Oz pleaded, "Think of me and the terrible trouble I'm in now that I've been found out." He explained, "No one else knows it but you four and myself. I fooled everyone for so long that I thought I'd never be discovered."
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹央求道：“想想我现在陷入的可怕麻烦吧，我已经被人发现了。”他解释说，“除了你们四人和我自己之外，没有人知道这件事。我骗了大家这么长时间，以为自己永远不会被揭穿。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy asked, "How did you appear to me as a great Head?"
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问道：“你出现时给我留下了怎样的巨大脑袋的印象？”

paragraphs.en: Oz led them into a small chamber behind the Throne Room. He pointed to a paper head with a painted face hanging from the ceiling by a wire. "This is how I made it appear alive," he explained, pulling a thread to make the eyes move and the mouth open.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹将他们带进宝座室后面的一间小房间。他指着天花板上挂着的一张画着脸的纸头，解释说：“这就是我让它看起来有生命的办法。”说着，他拉了根线，使眼睛动了起来，嘴巴也张开了。

paragraphs.en: "How did you manage the voice?" asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “你是怎么做到声音那么像的？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: "I am a ventriloquist," Oz replied. "I could throw my voice wherever I wanted, making you think it came from the head."
paragraphs.zh: “我是一名口技演员，”奥兹回答说，“我可以随意改变声音的位置，让你以为声音来自头部。”

paragraphs.en: He then showed them his disguise: the dress and mask he wore as the Lady, and the Tin Woodman saw that his Beast was just sewn skins with slats to keep their sides out. The Ball of Fire, hanging from the ceiling, turned out to be a ball of cotton set on fire by oil.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，他向他们展示了自己女巫装扮的伪装：那套服装和面具，以及铁皮人看到的那只“野兽”其实只是用皮革缝制而成，并用木条撑开身体两侧。悬挂在天花板上的火球，原来是用油脂点燃的一团棉花。

paragraphs.en: "Really," said the Scarecrow, "you should be ashamed for being such a humbug."
paragraphs.zh: “你真是个虚伪透顶的人，”稻草人说，“你应该为此感到羞耻。”

paragraphs.en: Oz admitted, sorrowfully, that he was indeed ashamed but had no other choice. He invited them to sit and told his story: born in Omaha, far from Kansas, he became a skilled ventriloquist before turning to balloonism.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹悲伤地承认自己确实感到羞愧，但别无选择。他请他们坐下，然后讲述了自己故事：他出生于奥马哈，远离堪萨斯州，曾是一名技艺高超的木偶戏演员，后来转向了热气球事业。

paragraphs.en: "Why did you give up the balloon?" Dorothy asked.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问道：“你为什么要放弃热气球？”

paragraphs.en: "I grew tired of it," Oz said. "Now I will tell you my whole story."
paragraphs.zh: “我对此感到厌倦了，”奥兹说，“现在我要把我的整个故事都告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: One day, Dorothy ascended in a balloon, only for the ropes to tangle, preventing her descent. The balloon soared high above the clouds, carried by an air current for miles. After a day and night, she landed in a strange country, where people mistook her for a great Wizard due to her unexpected arrival from the sky.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，多萝西乘着热气球升空，不料绳索缠绕在一起，阻止了她的下降。热气球被一股强劲的气流带着飞得极高，飘过了厚厚的云层，整整一夜，它在空中飞行了数里之遥。终于，在一个日夜之后，她降落在了一个陌生的国度，人们误以为她是从天而降的一位伟大的巫师。

paragraphs.en: To amuse herself and keep the people busy, Dorothy ordered them to build a city and palace. They complied willingly. She then named it the Emerald City, putting green spectacles on everyone so that everything appeared green to them.
paragraphs.zh: 为了自娱自乐并让这些人忙个不停，多萝西命令他们建造一座城市和宫殿。大家欣然遵从了她的命令。接着，她将这座城市命名为翡翠城，并给每个人戴上绿色的眼镜，使他们看到的一切都呈现出绿色。

paragraphs.en: Built many years ago, Oz, who was young when he arrived by balloon, is now an old man.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹是在热气球抵达时正值青春，这座建筑建于很多年前，如今他已经是一位老人了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy questioned, "Isn't everything here green?" Oz replied, "Yes, but with green glasses, naturally everything looks green." He explained that the city had been built long ago and that his people wore green spectacles so long they believed it to be truly emerald.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西疑惑地问道：“这里的一切不是都是绿色的吗？”奥兹回答说：“是的，不过戴上绿色眼镜后，自然 everything 都会看起来是绿色的。”他解释说这座城市很久以前就建成了，而他的子民们长期佩戴绿色眼镜，以至于他们相信这真的是翡翠色的。

paragraphs.en: Despite its beauty, filled with jewels and precious metals, Oz had shut himself away since the palace was constructed, refusing to see anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管奥兹国富丽堂皇，满是珠宝和珍贵金属，自宫殿建成以来，奥兹却一直闭门不出，拒绝见任何人。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy expressed her displeasure with the Wizard, calling him a bad man. The Wizard admitted to being a good person but a poor magician. Dorothy's companions sought his help: the Scarecrow wanted brains, and the Lion asked for courage.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西对巫师表达了不满，称他是个坏人。巫师承认自己是个好人，只是魔法不够高明。多萝西的同伴们向他求助：稻草人想要获得智慧，狮子则希望能得到勇气。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard promised to stuff the Scarecrow’s head with brains the next morning, though he could not teach how to use them effectively. Grateful, the Scarecrow vowed to find a way to utilize his newfound intelligence.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师承诺第二天早上会给稻草人填充智慧，虽然无法教会他如何有效运用这些智慧。稻草人感激不已，发誓要找到利用自己新获得的聪明才智的方法。

paragraphs.en: Concerned about his own bravery, the Lion questioned Oz further. The Wizard reassured him that courage is found in facing fear, which the Lion admitted he still felt despite having plenty of it.
paragraphs.zh: 为了验证自己的勇敢，狮子向奥兹进一步求证。巫师安慰他说，勇气在于面对恐惧，尽管狮子觉得自己并不缺乏这种感觉，但还是承认自己依然感到害怕。

paragraphs.en: Oz agreed to give the Tin Woodman a heart the next day. The Tin Woodman insisted on accepting the offer despite the potential unhappiness it might bring.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹答应第二天给铁皮人木偶一个心脏。尽管这个提议可能会带来一些不愉快，铁皮人坚持接受了这份馈赠。

paragraphs.en: "Very well," Oz meekly replied. "Come to me tomorrow, and you shall have a heart."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”奥兹谦卑地回答，“你明天再来找我吧，我会给你一颗心脏。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy then asked how they could return to Kansas. Oz suggested they would need to think about it for a few days before finding a solution.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西随后问道，她们该如何返回堪萨斯州。奥兹建议她们需要先思考几天，才能找到解决办法。

paragraphs.en: "That must be a matter of opinion," the Tin Woodman said. "I will bear all the unhappiness without complaint if I can get a heart."
paragraphs.zh: “这恐怕见仁见智了，”铁皮人说道，“只要能拥有一颗心，我愿意承受所有的不快乐而不抱怨。”

paragraphs.en: "Very well," Oz responded. "I have played Wizard long enough that I might as well continue the part a little longer."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”奥兹回答，“既然我已经当巫师很久了，不妨再演下去。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy proposed, "How am I to get back to Kansas?"
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问道：“我该怎么回到堪萨斯州呢？”

paragraphs.en: "We shall have to think about that," Oz replied.
paragraphs.zh: “我们得好好考虑一下这件事。”奥兹回答道。

paragraphs.en: For two days, they remained guests in the palace, where Oz's people served them and obeyed their every wish. In return for his help, Oz asked them to keep his secret—namely, that he was a humbug.
paragraphs.zh: 两天里，他们在宫殿中做客，奥兹的臣民们殷勤地伺候他们，并满足他们的每一个愿望。作为对他帮助的回报，奥兹要求他们保守一个秘密——即他不过是个骗子。

paragraphs.en: They agreed and returned to their rooms with high spirits. Dorothy hoped that "The Great and Terrible Humbug" would find a way to send her back home, and she was willing to forgive him if he did.
paragraphs.zh: 他们达成一致，带着高昂的情绪回到了各自的房间。多萝西希望“那伟大的可怕假象”能找到办法把她送回家，并且如果他能做到这一点的话，她愿意原谅他。
